description:
`fz-gk4` removed the only reader of the lazy-continuation descriptor's spec-id
slot: `fz_materialize_cont` used to pass it to `alloc_closure_slots` as a target
id the closure header discarded. Confirmed still true at main 417c5b0b5 -- both
reserved-hole comments are live:

    src/compiler2/native_codegen/closure.rs:222
        // +8 is a reserved hole: nothing reads it (fz-gk4).
    runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1833
        // +8 is reserved. It held the cont's spec id, which materialization passed to ...

`build_lazy_cont_descriptor` no longer writes it and `LAZY_CONT_SID_OFF` is gone,
so +8 is a documented hole inside a 32-byte header whose live fields are the code
pointer (+0) and the capture count (+16).

## Why it is not urgent

The descriptor is a STACK slot, so the waste is per mid-flight-yield frame rather
than heap-resident.

## Acceptance

Either compact the header -- watching the 16-byte alignment that
`LAZY_CONT_RAW_OFF = 32` currently guarantees -- or put a live field in the hole.
Either way the reserved-hole comments in both files go away, which is the
checkable part: a grep for "reserved" in those two locations should come back
empty.
title: Lazy cont descriptor carries a reserved 8-byte hole at +8
